title: Henri Matisse: 72 Years Ago Today, the Master Who Drew with Scissors Died

lines: He made masterpieces with scissors, from a wheelchair.
Who changed the world today? November 3.
Who changed the world today? November third.
72 years ago today, a painter died in Nice, France.
Seventy-two years ago today, a painter died in Nice, France.
He was Henri Matisse, the leader of the Fauves.

data.name: Matisse

lines: He began as a clerk in a law office.
At about twenty, appendicitis kept him in bed for a long time.
His mother brought him a box of paints,
and he left the law behind to become a painter.

items.caption: A mother's gift: a box of paints

lines: In 1905, he showed his work at the Autumn Salon in Paris,
In nineteen oh five, he showed his work at the Autumn Salon in Paris,
including a portrait of his wife in a hat.
The colours were so bold, a critic called them wild beasts,
and the name stuck: Fauvism.
Later, he painted for decades in sunny Nice.
For a Russian collector, he painted the huge Dance.

lines: In 1941, in his seventies, he had major surgery.
In nineteen forty-one, in his seventies, he had major surgery.
After that, he mostly worked from a wheelchair or from his bed.
He could no longer paint as before, so he picked up scissors.
He cut painted paper into leaves, stars and figures,
and called it drawing with scissors.
In 1947, he published a book of cut-outs called Jazz.
In nineteen forty-seven, he published a book of cut-outs called Jazz.
In his last years, he designed a small chapel in Vence,
from the stained glass to the wall drawings,
and he called it his masterpiece.
He died in Nice on November 3, 1954, at the age of eighty-four.
He died in Nice on November third, nineteen fifty-four, at the age of eighty-four.
His question for you:
if one day you could no longer do what you love the old way,
would you find a new way?
This is Who Changed the World Today,
and on November 3, we remember Henri Matisse.
